title: Two-scale filter-removal corridor
question: Can a low/high transition-energy split turn the s=1 frequency filter into an explicit finite filter-removal corridor whose low-frequency and high-frequency terms can be audited separately?

identity.resolvent_role: The corridor is a finite two-scale analogue of resolvent smoothing; a uniform common-core estimate and filter removal remain separate gates.

promotion_boundary: R-384 is a finite low/high transition-energy decomposition and filter-removal envelope check. It does not prove a cutoff-independent low-frequency bound, a Gibbs tail theorem, filter removal, common core, or any QFT closure.
next_action: Prove the corridor bounds on a Hamiltonian-derived common core with a cutoff- and source-independent low-frequency estimate and a resolvent-controlled high-frequency tail; otherwise register the first failed uniform premise.
boundary: Finite actual-Q3 edge and square matrices with all declared histories, reference filter s=1, and energy windows E=1,2,4. All source/volume/cutoff/beta uniformity, filter removal, common core, common alpha, KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A conclusions remain open.
